children: Apple's
event on Wednesday is widely seen as new CEO John Ternus' first major test, with the design veteran expected to herald a new era of innovation.
Ternus took the helm last week, at a time when Apple
is facing mounting pressure to maintain its edge in the AI race.
His keynote address at the event will set the tone for his vision of Apple's
future, according to Forrester analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee.

"Ternus inherits perhaps the most successful consumer technology juggernaut in modern times," Chatterjee said. "Tim Cook's perfected execution, scale, and monetization set a high bar, and Ternus must extend that run. But he must sustain that momentum while positioning Apple to disrupt itself in the near future."
One product that signals the new era is the foldable iPhone, which is among the most significant design changes for the smartphone.
Apple's
core technology development teams have been exploring foldable phones for almost a decade,
Bloomberg News
reported, citing sources.
Former CEO Tim Cook pushed for the foldable iPhone in 2020 after a trip to Asia, where people were using folding devices from Samsung
and other companies. Samsung launched its first Galaxy Fold in 2019.
Apple's
foldable device — iPhone Duo — will reportedly be priced starting at $2,000. That's more expensive than other foldable phones in the market.

But that may not deter buyers. "Even with a $2,500 price tag, the Apple foldable is ​going to fly off the shelves, especially because Apple is excellent at creating an aura of exclusivity, luxury, and scarcity," Nabila Popal, senior research director ​at IDC, told
Reuters
Other devices set to be unveiled at Wednesday's event include the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, new Apple Watches, and updated AirPods.
-- The Associated Press contributed to this report.
